top5.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a faster AI model
top5.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon on its paid API, Gemini app, and developer tools. The company says it is three times faster than Gemini 4 Carbon and outperforms Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on a reasoning benchmark.
top5.why: Google’s Gemini 4 Neon launch, covered by five newsletters, intensifies competition at the frontier of AI models and could shift enterprise developer and consumer demand.

top5.title: Anthropic carries out the largest IPO in history
top5.description: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq after raising $81.3 billion, surpassing the record set by SpaceX. The company is valued at $1.5 trillion despite reporting losses of $104 billion over nine months.
top5.why: Anthropic’s record $81.3 billion IPO and $1.5 trillion valuation make AI’s capital intensity and path to profitability a defining issue for public markets.

top5.title: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to China
top5.description: TSMC and Samsung have stopped shipping certain chips to Chinese customers after new US rules requiring licenses took effect. The measures also affect chips intended for non-AI uses, including smartphones.
top5.why: TSMC and Samsung halting some chip shipments to China shows that tightening U.S. export controls are disrupting global semiconductor supply beyond AI-specific products.

top5.title: The Java4Shell flaw exposes widely used enterprise applications
top5.description: Oracle has patched a Java vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated attackers to execute code or crash vulnerable systems. Researchers demonstrated attacks against Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Elasticsearch, with exposure depending on the Java version and processor configuration.
top5.why: The Java4Shell vulnerability creates immediate enterprise security risk because attackers can remotely compromise widely used platforms including Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Elasticsearch.

top5.title: Data center electricity consumption could double by 2030
top5.description: According to the International Energy Agency, data centers will consume twice as much electricity in 2030, with AI accounting for three-quarters of the increase. The sector’s carbon emissions could rise by 70% in four years.
top5.why: The IEA’s projection that data-center electricity consumption will double by 2030 highlights a major constraint for AI expansion, with implications for utilities, emissions, and infrastructure investment.
